**2B.6 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

Best-supported reading: **mixed, but leaning toward truthful/defensive public security framing rather than deliberate conflict-manipulating misinformation.** The clearest positive evidence is AMLO’s own de-escalatory crisis messaging and Mexico’s multilateral disarmament posture. The clearest negative evidence is domestic rhetoric and reform politics that critics saw as grievance-driven, fear-amplifying, and power-consolidating. I found **no direct 2024 evidence** of fabricated intelligence or explicit misinformation used to build support for war.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [La política se inventó para evitar la guerra, afirma presidente sobre conflicto en Medio Oriente](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/) | Presidente de México | 2024-04-13 | <https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/> | AMLO said politics exists to avoid war, warned against escalation in the Iran-Israel conflict, called war irrational and harmful, and urged peace and fraternity. This is direct evidence of a truthful, de-escalatory public explanation of security risk. | 2B.6, 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| [US, Mexico to clamp down on illegal immigration, leaders say](https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/) | Reuters | 2024-04-30 | <https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/> | Biden and AMLO agreed to coordinated steps to reduce irregular border crossings while protecting human rights. This is evidence of security threats being handled through concrete cooperation rather than fear-based escalation. | 2B.6, 2B.1, 2B.3 |
| [Foreign Ministry prioritizes nuclear disarmament on Mexico’s international agenda](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-02-14 | <https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en> | Mexico framed its diplomacy around a safer and more peaceful world grounded in international law and cooperation rather than weapons. This supports a pattern of public security messaging centered on restraint, not manufactured threat inflation. | 2B.6, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| [With World at Delicate Crossroads, Disarmament Committee’s Responsibility ‘Immense’, Says General Assembly President During Robust Debate](https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm) | United Nations, Meetings Coverage and Press Releases | 2024-10-08 | <https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm> | Mexico’s representative urged fewer warheads, more disarmament, and less rhetoric threatening nuclear use, while rejecting the idea that nuclear weapons are part of the solution. That is direct multilateral evidence of restrained, candid threat communication. | 2B.6, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| [Mexico’s final year marked by verbal attacks on journalists and rights advocates](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | <https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico> | The Reuters Institute described AMLO’s final year as marked by continued verbal attacks on journalists, human-rights advocates, and the media. This is negative evidence of a hostile rhetoric environment that can substitute for accurate public threat explanation. | 2B.6, 1B.8, 1B.9, 1B.10 |
| [Mexico: Proposed Constitutional Changes Threaten Rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-30 | <https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights> | HRW warned that AMLO’s proposed constitutional changes could weaken judicial independence, expand military power, and erode privacy safeguards. This is negative evidence that security language was sometimes tied to power-consolidation rather than transparent threat assessment. | 2B.6, 1B.7, 1B.9, 1B.10 |
| [Mexico's amnesty, legal protection reforms become law](https://theprint.in/world/mexicos-amnesty-legal-protection-reforms-become-law/2132532/) | Reuters | 2024-06-15 | <https://theprint.in/world/mexicos-amnesty-legal-protection-reforms-become-law/2132532/> | AMLO justified amnesty reforms partly by reference to cases like the 2014 Ayotzinapa disappearance, while critics said the package undercut victims’ rights and judicial safeguards. This is mixed evidence: grievance was used publicly, but the record does not show fabricated intelligence or open conflict-mongering. | 2B.6, 1B.7, 1B.10 |

**Bottom line**

- Best-supported conclusion: **AMLO mostly explained security threats in de-escalatory, institution-centered terms in 2024, especially on war-risk and border issues.**
- Counterevidence is mainly **domestic and indirect**: confrontational rhetoric toward critics, militarized reforms, and grievance-based justification of institutional changes.
- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** of deliberate misinformation, fake intelligence, or explicit fear-manufacturing to build support for conflict.

**Search gap**

- I did not find a 2024 source showing AMLO or his administration fabricating a threat narrative or using false intelligence to justify war or armed conflict.
- The available record is better read as **rhetorical polarization and power-consolidation criticism**, not clear conflict propaganda.
